title: Evidence Affinity Coalescer Agent — design & ops playbook
body:
Purpose and scope:

This document specifies the design, runtime behaviour, and operational runbook for the Evidence Affinity Coalescer Agent (EACA) — a mid-tier service that reduces noise and preserves high-value context when we export control evidence from collectors to downstream SIEM / forensic stores. EACA sits logically between the collector fleet and export pipelines.

Goals: 
- Reduce duplicate and near-duplicate artifacts that pollute SIEM and increase storage/ingest costs.
- Maintain cryptographic chain-of-custody and deterministic provenance metadata for grouped evidence.
- Attach RBAC v2 context snapshots (effective roles, token metadata) to coalesced artifacts.
- Provide idempotent export semantics and deterministic hashing for dedupe and replay safety.
- Offer sampling and coalescing configurations per-tenant, per-control, and per-source.

Non-goals: 
- Deep content redaction (left to collector plugins or export pipelines)
- Long-term archival storage (EACA emits to archive layer but does not persist beyond retention TTL in memory/disk cache)

Design overview:

1) Placement and flow:
- Collectors (edge/host/sidecar) tag events with a lightweight "affinity key" (see Affinity Key spec below).
- Events are forwarded to the EACA ingest endpoint (gRPC + HTTP fallback).
- EACA maintains per-affinity sliding windows, coalesces events, computes provenance envelopes, and emits a single coalesced artifact per-window to the evidence export bus (Kafka topic: evidence.coalesced).

2) Affinity key composition (deterministic, compact):
- source_id (collector id) OR hashed source cluster id
- control_id (rule/jira-like identifier for which control triggered)
- subject_fingerprint: stable fingerprint of the principal (userid/email/sha256), optionally hashed with tenant salt
- time_bucket (ISO minute window) — used as a hint for coalescing but not required for idempotency
- affinity_version: agent version to allow rolling changes
- Example key (concatenated): sha256(source|control|subject|v2)

3) Coalescing policy primitives:
- MAX_WINDOW_MS: hard limit for coalescing an affinity group (default 120000 ms)
- MAX_EVENTS: maximum events to coalesce before flush (default 100)
- SIZE_LIMIT_BYTES: max uncompressed payload size before partial flush (default 2MB)
- PRIORITY_EVICT: allow higher-severity events to force immediate emit
- SAMPLE_RATE: probabilistic sampler for low-value sources (per-tenant override)

4) Provenance envelope and audit-schema mapping:
- For a coalesced artifact, EACA produces: envelope_id (uuid), deterministic_coalesce_hash (sha256 over sorted canonicalized event fingerprints + agent salt + version), first_seen_timestamp, last_seen_timestamp, event_count, control_ids[], source_ids[], subject_snapshot (RBAC v2 effective roles + token_id), signed_manifest (ed25519 signature using KMS key id), mapping_version (audit_schema_v3).
- The manifest uses the standard internal audit-schema mapping. When exporting to SIEM formats (Elastic ECS / CEF), EACA attaches manifest fields under "redwood.evidence.manifest.*" and flattens subject_snapshot for indexing.

5) Idempotency and replay protection:
- Deterministic_coalesce_hash + envelope_id form the canonical dedupe key.
- Export pipeline stores last-seen hash for a short TTL (configurable per-exporter) to avoid duplicate ingestion on retries.
- When replaying collector logs, EACA will accept duplicates but will mark them as "replay_duplicated":true in the manifest if the dedupe hash already exists in downstream index.

Operational behaviour and runbook:

Start/Stop/Upgrade:
- EACA instances are stateless for long-term persistence; they keep short-lived disk-backed windows. Graceful drain: set drain=true via control-plane rollout API; new ingest is rejected and current windows are flushed.
- Rolling upgrade strategy: staggered pods, ensure per-pod active affinity windows < 90s during upgrade. Verify exported envelope rate before advancing.

Alerts (high priority):
- export-latency-p95 > 5s for >5m -> Pager (oncall-sre)
- coalesce-window-evictions-per-minute > 5% of ingested -> Pager
- signature-fails-per-minute > 0.1% -> Pager & security
- unexpected-ttl-expiry (windows lost due to memory pressure) -> Pager

Debugging checklist (typical incidents):
1) "Missing evidence" for a control
   - Check collector to confirm affinity key present (collector logs).
   - Query EACA metrics: active_windows_by_affinity, flush_rate, errors.
   - If windows truncated due to SIZE_LIMIT, review event size and consider increasing limit or enabling per-source sampling.

2) "Duplicate artifacts in SIEM"
   - Verify deterministic_coalesce_hash collisions (very unlikely) — check algorithm and agent salt.
   - Check downstream exporter dedupe cache TTL; if short, duplicates may reappear after TTL.

3) "Subject snapshot mismatches"
   - Confirm RBAC v2 fetcher response latency. A stale roles snapshot may have been attached; check token introspection logs.

Security and compliance considerations:
- All in-flight traffic to EACA must use mTLS and collector certs in the RBAC v2 allowlist.
- Signed manifests use KMS-managed keys with hardware-protected root (HSM recommended for production).
- Minimal PII in indexable fields: subject_snapshot contains role names and hashed principal ids by default. Tenant config can enable cleartext subject ids for legal/forensic reasons but must require approval.

Performance & resource guidance:
- Memory: default heap 1.5–2GB per 1000 events/s with default window sizes. Adjust upwards when increasing MAX_WINDOW_MS or SIZE_LIMIT_BYTES.
- CPU: coalescing hash and signature ops are CPU-bound; enable hardware-accelerated crypto on heavy tenants.
- Backpressure: when Kafka export lag > 30s, EACA will switch to aggressive flushing and drop non-critical samples (emit a metric and an audit event).

Testing and validation plan:
- Unit tests for deterministic coalesce hashing and fingerprints (edge cases: ordering, timestamp skew).
- Integration test harness that replays collector traces and validates 1:1 mapping of controls->coalesced envelopes under varying load and network delay.
- Fuzz tests for malformed affinity keys and maliciously large events.
- Privacy review: ensure subject hashing and salt rotation policies are tested for collision resistance.

Rollout phases:
- Canary (security lab tenants): 1% of traffic, monitor export fidelity and signature validation for 72h.
- Beta (internal tenants): 10% traffic, enable sigs + RBAC snapshots, gather feedback for TTL/size defaults.
- GA: full traffic, lock defaults, enable HSM signing.

Open questions and TODOs:
- [TODO] Decide default tenant salt rotation cadence and compat path for historical dedupe hashes.
- [Q] Should EACA perform semantic merge of JSON payloads for the same control, or just batch store original events? (Tradeoff: queryability vs fidelity.)
- [TODO] Integrate explicit per-tenant retention policy enforcement with the archived object storage lifecycle.

Appendix: example coalesce manifest (human-readable)
- envelope_id: eaca-20250203-01
- deterministic_coalesce_hash: sha256:abc123...
- first_seen: 2025-02-03T14:12:08Z
- last_seen: 2025-02-03T14:14:09Z
- event_count: 7
- control_ids: [SEC-LOGIN-FAIL, SEC-ACCOUNT-LOCK]
- subject_snapshot: { roles: [admin, billing-read], principal_hash: sha256:xyz }
- signature_kms_key: projects/redwood-kms/keys/eaca-prod-signing

If you are operating or testing EACA, please add incident notes to JIRA:SEC-8872 and link any export traces to CONFLUENCE:SEC-EVIDENCE-AFFINITY-OVERVIEW.

Notes to reviewers (informal):
- This is intentionally opinionated on deterministic hashing and signed manifests — we found earlier attempts that left deduping to downstream SIEMs caused very high ingest costs.
- Be ruthless on PII fields: prefer hashed identifiers unless explicit forensic flags are present.

End of playbook.
